description: Camera-agent browser runtime — getUserMedia video preview, canvas frame capture, multimodal LLM POST, overlay rendering of text + optional bounding boxes.

buildHints.whenToUse: Any product where the primary input is the device camera: visual QA, barcode/QR readers, OCR tools, 'describe what you see' agents, webcam-based search, live inspection apps.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on the configured port; the browser will prompt for camera permission on first visit.

The frontend is complete — focus on implementing the `/api/vision` backend described in `api/README.md`. Any multimodal LLM endpoint accepting `{ image: string, prompt: string }` and returning `{ answer: string }` works; `boxes` (bounding boxes) is optional.
Run `pnpm validate` to verify scaffold wiring without opening a browser — checks DOM IDs, API route, frame-capture call, and TypeScript syntax.
Run `pnpm build` to emit a static bundle to `dist/` — deploy to any static host; HTTPS is required for `getUserMedia` outside localhost.
gotchas: With `strict: true` in tsconfig, `document.getElementById()` returns `HTMLElement | null`. Every DOM query in `src/main.ts` uses an explicit `as` cast (e.g. `as HTMLVideoElement`). Without the cast, video/canvas/button-specific properties like `.videoWidth`, `.getContext()`, `.disabled` won't type-check.
The `/api` proxy in `vite.config.ts` is a dev-only convenience. In production, route `/api/*` through your deployment platform — Cloudflare Workers routes, Vercel rewrites, Nginx `proxy_pass`, etc.

`<canvas id="work" hidden>` in `index.html` is the off-screen frame-capture surface used by `captureFrame()` in `src/main.ts`. It is invisible by design. Removing it or changing its id breaks the capture flow.
architectureNotes: All browser logic lives in `src/main.ts` — camera lifecycle, frame capture, API call, and overlay rendering. Fork cleanly from there.
The hidden `#work` canvas captures frames off-screen; `#overlay` is the visible canvas that draws bounding boxes on top of the `#cam` video element. They serve different roles — don't merge them.
Bounding box coordinates from the API are normalized 0..1 so they survive display-size rescaling — multiply by `overlay.width`/`overlay.height` to get pixel coordinates.

placeholders.description: Bootstrap camera agent. Wire a real `/api/vision` backend (see `api/README.md`). Optionally replace the bounding-box overlay with custom rendering (heat maps, segmentation masks, etc.).
